_comment: Mike Schmidt Memorial Iron Team Award placings.
IMPORTANT: the award recognises the TOP THREE teams by cumulative score
across the three North American Baja SAE events in a season — not a single
winner. A team receiving the award has not necessarily won it. An earlier
version of this file recorded every sourced mention as a first place, which
silently promoted second and third places into wins.
Each entry therefore carries an explicit `place` (1, 2, 3, or null when the
source records a placing without saying which) and a `confidence`:
confirmed      independently sourced as that place
reported       a single team-history source states it; not corroborated
place-unknown  the team placed, but the source does not say where
unknown        nothing about that season is established
enumerate a team’s placings across many years, so a bare mention on one of
them is NOT evidence of a win. That is exactly how the earlier error crept in.
The season standings shown on the site are computed from SAE’s own archive by
total points and do not depend on this file at all. This is annotation.
Corrections welcome: open an issue or a PR against this file.

researchNotes.unknownYearsInvestigated: 2003, 2004, 2006, 2007, 2008 and 2011 were searched extensively across university news, team history pages and SAE articles without finding a winner. They are deliberately left blank rather than inferred.

ruledOut.rit: Won exactly three times — 2001, 2002, 2018 — per two RIT sources, so RIT did not win any of the unknown years.
ruledOut.cornell: Iron Team only in 2014 and 2025; the team was founded in 2003 and first competed in 2005.
ruledOut.michigan-tech: The 2009 win was reported as the first in school history, so Michigan Tech did not win 2003-2008.
